To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel network architecture for learning scene flow directly from 3D point clouds, and that it outperforms previous methods on both synthetic and real data.

we propose a new deep learning architecture for estimating scene flow from 3D point clouds, and we demonstrate that the architecture is capable of generalizing to real data and outperforms prior art on challenging benchmarks.

we introduce a new network for learning scene flow from point cloud data that generalizes from synthetic to real data and achieves competitive results to the state of the art, and that we demonstrate two applications of scene flow for point cloud data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three aspects: (1) a new learning layer for point sets, (2) an end-to-end learning network for 3D scene flow estimation, and (3) two applications of the network output.
the following questions. How to effectively learn hierarchical features of a dynamic scene from 3D point clouds? How to represent the motion of a point cloud and learn its embedding?

the following questions. How can we effectively learn deep representations of point clouds? Can we use deep learning to learn point cloud flow directly from point cloud data? What are the potential applications of such learned point cloud flow?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our FlowNet3D learns scene flow directly from unstructured 3D point clouds, and it outperforms previous approaches on both synthetic and real data.
our network is the first to learn scene flow from raw point clouds and achieves competitive results on both synthetic and real datasets, which shows its generalization and robustness.
our network learns to estimate scene flow in a 3D point cloud directly from the point cloud itself, and it is the first to achieve this in a fully end-to-end manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a deep learning framework for learning scene flow in point clouds and evaluate its performance on synthetic and real data, showing its potential for various applications.
, for the first time, we can estimate scene flow from point sets in a deep learning fashion.
we propose a deep neural network that can directly estimate scene flow from 3D point clouds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learning scene flow directly from unstructured point clouds is possible.
learning scene flow directly from 3D point clouds is feasible and promising, which is an important step towards understanding 3D dynamic scenes.
learning scene flow directly from 3D point clouds can be a powerful alternative to the traditional stereo based approaches.
